- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions at 5% of prior peak.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–5% downward bias to next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillations (e.g., +0.6, -0.4, +0.6), model may be overfitting; apply smoothing to forecast curve to reduce amplitude.
